lines: A hole... in a poor man's boat?
Prophet Musa, alayhis salaam, said: Have you torn it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing.
As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea. So I intended to cause defect in it, as there was after them a king who seized every ship by force.
The damage you can't understand today... may be what saves you.

scenes.style: High-quality 3D animated feature film still, close to photoreal (modern big-studio animation look), rich detail, cinematic lighting and depth of field. Vertical 9:16, keep the top third fairly simple and dark-to-plain (text sits there), the action in the lower two thirds. An ancient sea coast long ago. Absolutely no prophet or holy figure shown; no person close up.

scenes.s1: A small wooden fishing boat pulled up on a sunny shore with a fresh hole broken in its side planks, fishing nets beside it, bright morning. No people.
scenes.s2: A small wooden boat on a calm blue sea at dawn, water starting to seep through a broken plank, close view of the damaged hull. No people.
scenes.s3: Far out at sea, a line of large armed warships with dark sails approaching a coast, seen from the shore, ominous clouds. No people close.
scenes.s4: Fishermen's small boats with nets on a sunny harbour beach, the damaged boat among them left behind on the sand while big warships sail past in the distance. Small people from behind.
scenes.s5: A bright calm sea at sunrise with a small repaired fishing boat sailing safely, birds over the water, hopeful golden light. ABSOLUTELY NO PEOPLE, no human figures, no silhouettes on the shore or in the boat.
